question: Automatic black (DefaultBlackRender Auto) on night scenes of the EOS 60D: tones and colour of the deepest blacks against Lightroom

protocol.lightroom: Camera Neutral, sharpening and noise 0, lens off, sRGB 16-bit, exported by the user 2026-11-15 (tests/image/base/neutre/<scene>-2.tif); day scenes from Pictures/RAW/Oliana
protocol.ipr: iprRenderServer in memory, neutral state; variants set by temporary environment switches, removed after the choice
protocol.metrics: L* percentiles, share of pixels below L* 2, mean CIE chroma; no registration (distributions)

variants.luma: 0.005 on the luminance, channel ratios kept
variants.toe1: 0.005, per channel, toe from 0 to twice the black (chosen)

choice: toe1: day scenes unchanged (within 0.01 L*), night scenes keep more colour (chroma 0.12-0.36 against 0.01-0.13; Lightroom 0.6-1.6) and slightly more light
limits: Lightroom keeps night scenes lighter and more colourful than any fixed black: it seems to adapt its black to the scene; not reproduced
no automatic black gives Lightroom-like chroma but too light night scenes and lifted day shadows (+4 L*, 15 November)
